title: Long-tail profile compatibility and safety-net for verified performance profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: As we onboard more model variants and hardware profiles, a subset of published 'Redwood-verified' performance profiles become stale or incompatible with new runtime kernel/quantization combinations. This causes subtle regressions for Dedicated and Private customers who have pinned to a profile. Goal: Design and implement a compatibility and safety-net layer that prevents pinned profiles from causing production regressions while preserving the auditability and cryptographic signing of published profiles. Deliverables: 1) a compatibility check that runs pre-publish and periodically post-publish; 2) a 'graceful ghosting' mechanism to mark profiles as deprecated without breaking pins; 3) an automated, sampled backfill shadow validation job that generates candidate replacement profiles; 4) admin UI and APIs for profile restore, sign-off, and emergency rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-publish compatibility check added to publishing pipeline and fails publish for critical incompatibilities
Periodic post-publish scanner runs nightly and flags profiles with significant latency/cost drift (>20% median change) or kernel failures
Graceful ghosting marks profiles as 'Deprecated (ghosted)' and triggers automatic fallback mapping for pinned customers
Shadow-validation job can produce a candidate profile within 6 hours for high-traffic models and attach a cost/latency delta summary
Console shows a clear restore/rollback flow and exposes signed manifest metadata; SRE runbook updated
No customer-facing disruption during staged canary of safety-net for Dedicated customers (verified via canary metrics)
End-to-end tests and a GitHub PR are merged and code reviewed (links in comments)
proposed_solution: 1) Extend the publishing pipeline to include a binary compatibility matrix check (model architecture x quantization x kernel capability). 2) Implement a nightly 'profile health scanner' that uses sampled production traces to re-run representative microbenchmarks and compares signatures. 3) Introduce 'ghost' state for profiles: metadata change + signed tombstone that preserves pin resolvability but signals consoles/APIs to route to fallback variants. 4) Create a 'shadow backfill' worker that, when a profile is flagged, launches targeted microbench bundles across representative hardware and emits candidate replacement profiles with cost/latency deltas. 5) Add console and API controls for steward sign-off and emergency un-ghosting. 6) Implement telemetry: profile-change events, rollback counts, customer fallback counts, and SLO impact metrics.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): prototype pre-publish compatibility checks in staging and surface failures to publishing engineers. Phase 2 (3 weeks): build nightly scanner and basic ghost metadata; start shadow backfill for top-50 models only. Phase 3 (3 weeks): integrate fallback mapping, console UI for profile state, and automated sign-off flow. Phase 4 (2 weeks): canary in Hosted then Dedicated customers with low blast radius, run for 2 weeks, measure regressions. Phase 5: full rollout and postmortem. Communication: customer advisory for Dedicated customers with pinned profiles and opt-in pilot for restoration.
risks: Automated ghosting could be overly conservative and cause unnecessary fallbacks, increasing token cost
Shadow backfill jobs may increase infra spend if not throttled correctly
Maintaining cryptographic signature chain while allowing tombstones needs careful design to avoid replay attacks
Misclassification of transient noise as drift may trigger churn on profiles
Console UX could be confusing and prompt unsafe manual restores without evidence
